original_target.title: Néel order in the square-lattice spin-one-half antiferromagnet

full_original_statement:
For even $`L\ge4`$, let $`\Lambda_L=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^2`$. At every site put spin operators $`S_x^a=\sigma_x^a/2`$, where

```math
\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad\sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
```

Let $`\psi_L`$ be the normalized ground state of

```math
H_L=\sum_{\{x,y\}\text{ nearest neighbors}}\sum_{a=1}^3S_x^aS_y^a
```

on $`\bigotimes_{x\in\Lambda_L}\mathbb C^2`$, with each bond counted once. Set $`\eta_x=(-1)^{x_1+x_2}`$. Prove or disprove

```math
\liminf_{\substack{L\to\infty\\L\text{ even}}}\frac1{L^4}\sum_{x,y\in\Lambda_L}\eta_x\eta_y\langle\psi_L,\mathbf S_x\cdot\mathbf S_y\psi_L\rangle>0.
```

sources.scope_comparison: The target is an unconditional strictly positive liminf of the ground-state averaged staggered structure factor for the isotropic spin1/2 square lattice. The actual Low body uses rigorous inequalities but inserts Monte-Carlo short-distance correlations with statistical errors to show their violation. Those sampled bounds are not certified deterministic input, so the paper does not supply an unconditional proof. Higher spin/dimension, anisotropic or AKLT statements are different Hamiltonians.
